the ablation of C9orf2 in the background of excitotoxicity induced ALS in rats.

the loss of C9ORF72 protein alone does not cause ALS in rats, but it does increase the vulnerability of MNs to other ALS risk factors, such as glutamate excitotoxicity, and thus may contribute to the development of ALS.
